title: needs-decision: no bundle sharing idd-overview-core has headroom for the token-cost-report wiring
body:
# needs-decision: no bundle sharing idd-overview-core has headroom for the token-cost-report wiring

## Background

Refs #2296. That roadmap's 5th success criterion --
`node scripts/token-cost-report.mjs --check` becoming part of this
repository's dogfood validate commands -- requires adding
`&& node scripts/token-cost-report.mjs --check` (~44 bytes) to the
**pre-push-validate** row's command string in
`idd-overview-core.instructions.md`'s Project commands table (the only
place that command chain is defined; `docs/token-cost.md`'s own "How
the snapshot is produced" section already documents this as deferred
for exactly this reason).

`idd-overview-core.instructions.md` (with `idd-overview-appendix
.instructions.md`) is a shared preamble across **five** context-ceiling
bundles (`audit/sync-manifest.json`), and on current `main`
(`b92f762c`, 2026-09-03) every one of them sits at or above the 98%
`maxUtilizationPct` hard-fail threshold or within a few dozen bytes of
it:

| Bundle | Files | limitBytes | Live utilization (`node scripts/audit-docs.mjs --check`) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bundle-discovery` | +`idd-claim`, `idd-discover`, `idd-suitability` | 109,700 | 95.48% |
| `bundle-resume` | +`idd-resume` | 45,000 | 96.30% |
| `bundle-work` | +`idd-work` | 49,500 | 97.90% |
| `bundle-review` | +`idd-advisory-wait`, `idd-ci`, `idd-review-fix`, `idd-review-snapshot`, `idd-review-triage` | 138,000 | 97.87% |
| `bundle-merge` | +`idd-advisory-wait`, `idd-ci`, `idd-merge-handoff`, `idd-merge`, `idd-pre-merge` | 122,000 | 98.00% |

Verified empirically, not just estimated from the percentages above:
adding the exact candidate string to `idd-overview-core
.instructions.md`'s pre-push-validate row and re-running
`node scripts/audit-docs.mjs --check` immediately fails with
`bundle-merge utilization 98.04% exceeds 98% (119605/122000 bytes)` --
a hard CI failure, not a notice. `bundle-merge` already sat at exactly
98.00% before this change (zero headroom under the hard-fail line), so
any addition to a file it shares trips it first.

This is the same class of problem #2377 already resolved for
`bundle-work` specifically (raising its `limitBytes` 45,000 -> 49,500,
closed 2026-09-03) -- but that decision did not, and could not, cover
`bundle-merge`, `bundle-review`, `bundle-resume`, or `bundle-discovery`,
each a separate `limitBytes` under the shared 196,000-byte
`maxBundleLimitBytes` ceiling. Per this repository's established
practice (#2091, #2181, #2377), the amount and
whether-to-raise-vs-trim-vs-relocate decision for a shared bundle is a
maintainer call, not one an autonomous session should make unilaterally
against a shared policy constant (`docs/policy-constants.md`).

## Proposed change

No single proposed change: this is a maintainer decision among the
options below, the same pattern #2091, #2181, and #2377 used for the
same class of problem.

### Options for a maintainer to choose among

1. **Raise the tightest affected bundle's (`bundle-merge`) `limitBytes`**
   (currently 122,000) enough to restore working headroom across all
   five affected bundles, mirroring #2377's `bundle-work` fix. All five
   bundles above have room under the 196,000-byte ceiling for this.
2. **Trim existing content** in `idd-overview-core.instructions.md` or
   `idd-overview-appendix.instructions.md` to fund the new command
   reference without raising any `limitBytes` -- requires a maintainer
   (or an explicitly maintainer-scoped follow-up issue) to choose what
   substantive content to cut from a file shared by every IDD phase.
3. **Document the new validate step somewhere other than the shared
   Project commands table** -- for example a source-repo-only doc that
   is not part of any budgeted bundle -- if the maintainer judges that
   still satisfies "part of this repository's dogfood validate
   commands." This changes the criterion's interpretation, not just its
   placement, so it needs the same sign-off as the other options.
4. **Accept the permanent deferral**: leave `docs/token-cost.md`'s
   existing deferred-wiring note as the final state and treat roadmap
   #2296's 5th criterion as satisfied by "verified drift-free but not
   wired into an automated gate," closing the roadmap on that basis.
5. **Something else the maintainer prefers.**

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A maintainer states which option above to take (or a different
      resolution) in a comment on this issue.
- [ ] Close this issue once that decision is recorded. The chosen
      option becomes a follow-up `ready` issue scoped to the exact
      manifest/content/doc change, mirroring how #2091, #2181, and
      #2377 were resolved -- this issue itself stays decision-only.

## Impact

This is the sole remaining blocker on roadmap #2296's 5 success
criteria (the other 4 are met per the 2026-09-03 A1.5 re-audit). The
roadmap stays open with `status:needs-decision` until this resolves.

---

_Autopilot suitability: 4 / 5 -- higher is more autopilot-suitable;
below the configured floor is human-oriented. This is a policy/capacity
trade-off; the field evidence above is settled and does not need
re-deriving._
